key_insight: Understanding what people need and choosing how to respond are different skills. PsycheMME evaluates them separately in videos, revealing distinctions that a single overall accuracy score can hide.
problem_solved: Aggregate benchmark scores can obscure whether an AI struggles to understand a social situation or to select an appropriate response.
method: Organize evaluation around eight capabilities spanning grounding, states, needs, interaction decisions, memory, and risk.
Use Social Information Processing and the Perception-Action Cycle to distinguish human understanding from response selection.
impact: PsycheMME offers practitioners a framework for diagnosing social-understanding and response-selection capabilities separately. This can help target improvements in video-based AI assistants beyond overall accuracy.
visual_elements: Two-stage flow diagram: understand the person → select a response.
Capability wheel showing the eight-capability framework, grouped by the areas named in the abstract.
Dataset count cards: 630 video episodes and 1,000 questions.
Conceptual comparison of one aggregate score versus a capability-level scorecard, without implying reported results.
paper_title: PsycheMME: A Psychology-Informed Benchmark for Social Understanding and Interaction in Videos
paper_authors: Heran Hu, Yuhang Dong, Zhucun Xue, Kaiwei Chen, Yong Liu
